questions.questionText: Three warehouse lookups take 2 seconds each. Why does the async version finish in about 2 seconds?
questions.explanation:
Run one after another, the lookups cost about 6 seconds. Async lets them run at the same time.

(A) Async does not speed up each lookup. Each one still waits 2 seconds, but the waits overlap.

(C) The request names east, west and central. Async changes how the calls run, not which ones are made.

options.optionText: Each lookup gets faster on its own.
The waits overlap, so the lookups run in parallel instead of one after another.
The agent skips the warehouses that are not named in the request.

questions.questionText: What does `await asyncio.sleep(2)` stand for in `check_warehouse_inventory`?
questions.explanation:
The code comment says so: the sleep is a stand-in for a real warehouse API call.

(B) No prompt appears in this code. The sleep is a pause, not a question.

(C) Nothing is cancelled. The lookup returns its data after the wait.

options.optionText: A delay that simulates a slow API call.
A prompt that asks you to confirm the lookup.
A timeout that cancels the lookup after 2 seconds.
